tasks.title: Backend gap 2 — super-chain.yml workflow_run default-branch restriction: confirm pinned-SHA dispatches don't fire the trigger; fix correctly
tasks.notes: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED + FIX (session-22, 2026-09-13). The operator's pinned-SHA-default-branch hypothesis is DISPROVEN: (1) dispatch.mjs dispatchWorkflow passes ref=DEFAULT_BRANCH ('main'); (2) code_ref is an INPUT, not the dispatch ref; (3) live run 34772202301 (cat-p1) has head_branch='main', event='workflow_dispatch', conclusion='success'; (4) stage-b.yml's name byte-matches super-chain.yml's workflows[] entry; (5) default_branch='main'. So all prerequisites for workflow_run ARE met — yet super-chain.yml's ONLY 2 runs are BOTH event=workflow_dispatch (manual session-19 diagnostics); it has NEVER auto-fired. CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE: the chained super part dispatches with code_ref = currentBranchSha() = main HEAD SHA, which makes stage-b.yml CHECK OUT THAT EXACT SHA — which is exactly github.sha (the commit that triggered the run). github.sha is NEVER BEHIND the checked-out SHA, so stage-b.yml NEVER commits the final status.json change (git commit reports 'nothing to commit', then refuses the empty push). status.json therefore stays 'stage_b_running', so super-chain's own gate (status.state=='complete') never passes even if workflow_run fired. FIX (applied in motionssalt/clipforge): (a) stage-b.yml now unconditionally force-writes jobs/<job>/status.json to state=complete at the end (checkout default branch, write via a tiny Python call to pipeline.status with --force, commit with -a, push) so the completion event always persists state=complete; (b) super-chain.yml made robust: still triggers on workflow_run (primary), but the status gate now ALSO accepts the workflow_run conclusion success (not solely status.json), so a genuine completed run chains the next part even if a status write raced. This preserves the SHA-pin (needed for restart-correctness) while removing the empty-commit break. LIVE-VERIFIED below in task-96.

tasks.title: Investigate slow scene-detect run: source video duration/resolution/bitrate vs typical 2-3min runs (instruction Part 1.1)
tasks.notes: DONE (session-24, 2026-09-13) — slow run IDENTIFIED and explained by source characteristics; NO code regression. Slow run = stage-a.yml run 34783277244 (job manual-1789333712217, 2026-09-13 21:15-21:53Z, 37.5min total; the ONLY run whose 'Local vision-assist stack' step exceeded 20min). TYPICAL PRIOR RUN for comparison = run 34721145161 (manual-1789249757677, vision step 2-3min): original.mkv = 1314.647s (21.9 min), 1920x1080 (FHD) HEVC Main-10 23.81fps, 1732 kb/s. tasks.title: Live progress visibility for vision-assist ffmpeg passes (instruction Part 1.3) — NO timeout/kill switch
tasks.notes: DONE (session-24) — motionssalt/clipforge commit f1515653, pushed + verified on origin/main. New run_ffmpeg_streaming() in pipeline/stage_a/scenes.py replaces subprocess.run(capture_output=True, text=True) at BOTH long single-pass decode call sites: detect_shots (scene-detect pass) and extract_baseline_composites (fps=1 tile pass) — the two passes observed running 9m50s/13m09s with zero output in slow run 34783277244. Implementation: Popen(stderr=PIPE, text mode, bufsize=1), reads stderr incrementally, splits CR/LF (ffmpeg stats use carriage returns), prints compact frame=/time= heartbeat lines throttled to ~1 per 32 chunks plus 1-in-25 sampled showinfo frame lines, returns (complete_stderr, returncode) exactly as capture_output would have provided. NO timeout=, NO kill switch, NO elapsed-time abort anywhere — proc.wait() blocks until the process exits however long it takes (instruction Part 1.2 honored verbatim). Scope decisions: emit_event_composite (line ~484) left on capture_output intentionally — it is a bounded 4-second-window pass (~1-3s each) that already prints a live per-composite line after every file ('event composite [start] @ 6.51s -> ...' seen every ~2s in the slow run's log), so it never had the no-visibility problem. ingest.py file/ffprobe container-sniff calls are instant probes, not decodes; bundle.py runs the python prompt generator, not ffmpeg. Both out of scope. NOTE: pipeline/stage_b/reframe.py carries its own identical detect_shots copy (line 82) with the same capture_output pattern, but it belongs to the Stage B cinematic-reframe path, NOT the 'Local vision-assist stack' step the instruction scopes to ('check scenes.py fully') — left untouched; flagged here for a future session if Stage B reframe ever shows the same symptom.
